e: From West African languages, such as Lingala fufú (“white-white”).
Borrowed from Japanese ふふ (fufu, onomatopoeia for laughter).
q: Africans generally serve highly seasoned stews with a starch - corn, millet, yams, cassava or rice - which they mash and whip to a paste, called fufu in West Africa. This is topped with a sauce known as palava.
[1987 July 29, Steven Barboza, “Culinary Delights of Africa Reflect a Continent's Diversity”, in The New York Times, →ISSN:
